summary: Users see 401 invalid_token on ~36% of auth-service token validations starting 14:02:22Z, a stable plateau that also drives api-gateway to ~21% errors. Onset is tightly bracketed by two coincident auth-service changes: code deploy dep-5710 (v7.3.0, jjwt 0.11->0.12 breaking parser API, TokenValidator rewritten) at 14:00:00Z and config change cfg-2705 (jwt signing key rotation k-2025-10 -> k-2026-04) at 14:01:00Z. All resource, latency, restart, rate-limit and redis-cache metrics are flat, ruling out resource exhaustion, capacity saturation, and dependency failure; market-data-service's earlier 11:35 deploy is unrelated (unaffected). Both remaining hypotheses (bad_deployment from the JWT library rewrite vs config_change from the signing-key rotation) are plausible and cannot be separated because auth-service's own logs are unavailable (503 log-pipeline outage), so signature/key-id failures cannot be distinguished from parser/validation failures. Outcome is inconclusive; the two candidate triggers are identified and all alternatives ruled out.

ranked_hypotheses.title: auth-service v7.3.0 JWT library upgrade broke token validation for a subset of tokens
ranked_hypotheses.statement: dep-5710 (v7.3.0, 14:00) upgraded jjwt 0.11->0.12 with a breaking parser API and rewrote TokenValidator; the rewritten validation logic rejects a stable ~36% of otherwise-valid tokens, returning 401 invalid_token, matching the HIST-109 pattern (JWT library upgrade changed clock-skew default).

causal_chain.claim: JWT parser API change / rewritten TokenValidator alters validation behavior
a subset of tokens fails validation -> 401 invalid_token beginning 14:02:22Z

assumptions: The jjwt 0.12 parser rewrite actually changed acceptance behavior for a token subset (e.g. clock-skew, claim/alg handling).
Onset is caused by this deploy rather than the key rotation 1 minute later.

ranked_hypotheses.title: auth-service signing-key rotation (cfg-2705) not fully propagated caused 401s
ranked_hypotheses.statement: cfg-2705 (14:01) rotated jwt.signing.key_id k-2025-10 -> k-2026-04; the new key id was published before all auth-service pods/consumers loaded the corresponding key material (JWKS), so tokens under the old/new key id are rejected, returning 401 invalid_token, matching HIST-108.

causal_chain.claim: new key id propagated inconsistently across validation paths
tokens failing signature/key-id check -> 401 invalid_token from 14:02:22Z

assumptions: Key material for k-2026-04 was not available on all verification paths at 14:01-14:02.
Onset is caused by this rotation rather than the deploy 1 minute earlier.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Dependency (redis-cache / key material store) failure
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A shared dependency (redis-cache) failed and caused validation failures.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: redis-cache hit_ratio_pct is flat ~96% and healthy across the window (F9); no evidence of cache or dependency fault.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Resource exhaustion / capacity saturation at auth-service
ranked_hypotheses.statement: auth-service ran out of CPU/memory/connections and failed requests.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: CPU (~38%), memory (~52%), latency (~90ms), rate-limit (~2/min) and restarts (0) are all flat across onset (F6); request_rate is steady ~400/s with no load spike (capacity ruled out).

facts.statement: auth-service 5xx error rate rose from ~0.2% to a stable ~36% starting in the 14:00 bucket, coincident with the incident onset.
401 invalid_token responses on POST /v1/token/validate begin at 14:02:22Z and persist, seen in api-gateway logs at WARN level.
api-gateway, the sole upstream caller of auth-service, degrades in lockstep to ~21% error rate.
auth-service received a JWT library upgrade deploy (dep-5710, v7.3.0) at 14:00:00Z that rewrote TokenValidator with a breaking parser API.
auth-service signing key_id was rotated (cfg-2705) at 14:01:00Z from k-2025-10 to k-2026-04.
auth-service showed no CPU, memory, latency, rate-limit or restart anomalies at onset.
market-data-service, which deployed earlier at 11:35, was unaffected (error rate flat ~0.2%), excluding its deploy as a cause.
auth-service application logs were unretrievable (503), preventing discrimination between failure modes.
redis-cache, an auth-service dependency, remained healthy (hit ratio ~96%), excluding a cache dependency failure.

timeline.event: market-data-service deploys v5.0.3 (unrelated; service stays healthy).
auth-service deploys v7.3.0 (dep-5710): jjwt 0.11->0.12, TokenValidator rewritten.
auth-service config change cfg-2705 rotates jwt.signing.key_id k-2025-10 -> k-2026-04.
First 401 invalid_token on auth-service /v1/token/validate appears in api-gateway logs.
auth-service error rate reads ~36%, api-gateway ~21%; incident reported as INC-007.
Error rate still ~36% (no self-recovery), deploy remains live and not rolled back.

recommended_actions.action: Obtain the actual auth-service validation error detail (exception class/message) via direct pod access or log shipping bypass, to distinguish signature/key-id failure from parser/validation failure.
recommended_actions.rationale: This single piece of evidence separates H1 from H2; auth-service logs are currently unretrievable (503).

recommended_actions.action: If the failure is a recent regression, roll back dep-5710 (v7.3.0 -> previous version) and measure whether 401s recover.
recommended_actions.rationale: Fastest test of the bad_deployment hypothesis; HIST-109 was resolved by rollback.

recommended_actions.action: Re-publish/restore the previous signing key (k-2025-10) and confirm JWKS propagation to all validation paths as an independent test of cfg-2705.
recommended_actions.rationale: Directly tests the config_change hypothesis; HIST-108 resolution was re-publishing the previous key.

recommended_actions.action: Decouple future deploys from scheduled key rotations (do not ship both in the same minute) and stage key rotations with propagated JWKS.
recommended_actions.rationale: The two coincident changes are what makes this incident ambiguous.

recommended_actions.action: Restore the identity-namespace log pipeline and add alerting that fires specifically on invalid_token rate.
recommended_actions.rationale: Log outage blocked root-cause determination and onset detection was delayed to the report.

data_gaps: auth-service application logs (and any JWKS/key-load messages) are unretrievable due to the identity-namespace log-pipeline outage (503), so the precise validation failure mode is unknown.
No visibility into per-pod rollout state for dep-5710 vs the timing of keyset propagation for cfg-2705, so the two triggers cannot be temporally separated below the 1-minute gap.
No metric decomposes the 36% failures by token issuer/key-id/version, which would directly attribute failures to key-id vs parser behavior.

findings.statement: auth-service HTTP 5xx error rate jumps from ~0.2% to ~36% in the 14:00 bucket and stays on a stable ~36% plateau through 15:48; pre-onset buckets 13:00-13:48 are all ~0.2%.
api-gateway logs show 401 invalid_token on auth-service POST /v1/token/validate beginning at 14:02:22Z; all entries are level WARN (no ERROR), and the same pattern persists at least to 15:58:51Z.
api-gateway (the only upstream caller of auth-service) also degrades at the same time: error_rate goes from ~0.2% to ~21% starting in the 14:00 bucket.
Code deploy dep-5710 to auth-service v7.3.0 at 14:00:00Z (author d.verma) upgraded jjwt 0.11->0.12 with a breaking parser API and rewrote TokenValidator; status is live and rolled_back_at is null.
Config change cfg-2705 rotated auth-service jwt.signing.key_id from k-2025-10 to k-2026-04 at 14:01:00Z, described as a scheduled signing-key rotation executed by security-automation.

auth-service shows no resource pressure at onset: cpu_pct stays ~38%, memory_pct ~52%, latency_p99_ms ~90ms, rate_limited_per_min ~2/min, request_rate ~400 req/s, and restarts remain 0 throughout the window.
market-data-service (which deployed v5.0.3 at 11:35:00Z, before onset) is completely unaffected; its error_rate stays ~0.2% across the whole window from 13:00 to 15:48.
auth-service logs are unsearchable: query_logs against auth-service returned backend unavailable (503) after 3 attempts (matching the reported log-pipeline outage).
redis-cache (an auth-service dependency) shows no degradation at onset: hit_ratio_pct stays ~96% across the window.

Historical incident HIST-109 (2025-07-11) was a token-validation regression with identical symptoms (401 invalid_token) caused by a JWT library upgrade changing the clock-skew default (bad_deployment), resolved by rollback. HIST-108 (2025-10-01) was 401s after signing-key rotation caused by publishing a new key id before all pods loaded the JWKS (config_change).

refs.quote: JWT library upgrade changed clock-skew default
Key rotation published new key id before all pods loaded the JWKS

findings.statement: Only two changes to any service in the incident window (auth-service dep-5710 at 14:00 and cfg-2705 at 14:01); no other service deployed or changed config between 13:00 and 15:59.

Because both candidate changes touch token validation within 1 minute of each other and the auth-service application logs (which would show whether failures are signature/verification errors vs parse/validation errors) are unretrievable, the two hypotheses cannot be separated from telemetry alone.

The stable ~36% plateau (not 0% or 100%, no ramp) is consistent with a fixed subset of tokens failing under either a rewritten validator or a partially propagated signing-key rotation, and does not by itself discriminate between them.
